text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Ministry of science and technology plans to distribute 5,000 scholarships to university students over the next five years, says Ivan Mandic of Education Ministry.
- Present business facility tenants will have advantage when extending their contracts only if they accept initial price set by the government.
- Police will reinforce traffic patrols this Friday and Saturday afternoon following six traffic-related deaths last weekend.
- Zagrebacka Banka will offer custody service to domestic clients by the summer. Such service was so far available only for foreigners.
- Government proposes law limiting number of gambling houses in Croatia to maximum of eight.
- Commentary: Oil concern INA needs to invest $600 million to modernise dated refineries in the next few years if it wants to win back some markets in neighbouring countries.
- State will extend additional 70,000 kuna loans from budget for cattle breeders to boost production ahead of tourist season, Agriculture Minister Zlatko Dominikovic says.
- Two hundred high-school professors in Zagreb protest, demanding better wages and working conditions.
- Pensioners' trade unions demand that State Statistics Institute review methods of estimating living costs which determine their income.
- Food concern Podravka expands sales in Australia and New Zealand and plans spread to Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines and Singapore, says Jasna Mujadzic, company representative in Sydney.
